title: Red Sea risk advances from prospective offensive to confirmed kinetic escalation
net_new_delta: Relative to durable event 20261002T211139Z_macro_red_sea_escalation_risk.json, Yemen's internationally recognized government reports 20 airstrikes on Houthi targets in Taiz within three hours. This confirms a kinetic escalation but does not establish Bab el-Mandeb closure or realized energy supply disruption.
fact: Yemen's internationally recognized government reported 20 airstrikes on Houthi personnel, movements, vehicles and military equipment in Taiz province within three hours.
Brent settled October 2 at $102.25/bbl and WTI at $91.11 after Europe agreed emergency diesel/crude stock releases; market pricing does not confirm a new realized supply shock.
source_claim: Reuters characterizes the Taiz strikes as a significant escalation after the relative lull associated with the 2022 truce.
Reuters reports Saudi Arabia is preparing a larger Saudi-backed operation intended to regain control around Bab el-Mandeb, expected within weeks.
model_inference: Promote RED_SEA_ESCALATION_RISK from PROSPECTIVE to CONFIRMED_KINETIC_ESCALATION, while retaining REALIZED_ENERGY_SUPPLY_DISRUPTION as unconfirmed.
unknown: Whether fighting reaches Bab el-Mandeb/coastal infrastructure.
Whether maritime traffic, freight, insurance or physical petroleum flows are measurably impaired.
Whether the broader Saudi-backed offensive launches and persists.
conflicts: Military escalation is becoming more concrete while emergency stock releases and current crude settlements do not confirm a fresh physical supply shock.
next_decisive_check: Require operational evidence connecting fighting to Bab el-Mandeb/coastal infrastructure plus measurable maritime/freight/refined-product deterioration despite emergency stock releases.

evidence.topic: Oil settlement and emergency stock releases

oracle.finding: Confirmed Taiz airstrikes justify upgrading Red Sea risk from prospective to kinetic escalation, but not to realized energy-supply disruption.

supermesh_x.finding: Fresh Reuters military evidence and energy-market evidence remain causally distinct: escalation is confirmed while crude pricing/emergency releases do not verify maritime or physical supply impairment.
